knownGaps.text: A question without "?" ("what should I name my app") is not treated as a question, so a task read out of it can still be stored.

Other question shapes slip through: "Which is better, Vue or React Native?" names a multi-word Title Case name and reaches the model; an impersonal question about your project that starts like a definition ("What is Trail Tracker's next milestone?") is dropped.
"We ..." at the start of an indented line after a shell prompt is dropped unless the line names a multi-word Title Case name ("We moved it to Go" is dropped).
A prose line ending in a space and a backslash is dropped with the next line.
Non-indented tool output after a $ prompt is dropped only when it matches a known pattern (git, Go panics, log levels, source locations); other output lines reach the model.
The secret-talk rule is pattern-based. It still drops some honest facts ("the user's JWT tokens expire hourly" reads as owning a token; "CSRF_TOKEN is set per request" names a credential variable).

Masking a value to the end of its clause can over-mask: in "my password is hunter2 for Trail Tracker" the words "for Trail Tracker" are masked too. The model never sees them, and the post-filter withholds them, so a Trail Tracker node from that message is lost (measured by test_over_masking_loss_is_counted_not_silent and a strict xfail). The drop is counted in the extraction result's dropped total, not itemised. If the name appears anywhere else in the message, the node is kept.

Secret masking, what it covers. Verified forms only: the exact examples in Handled forms (tested), with only the secret value changed to another value of the same kind, at least the row's minimum length and within its case limit. A form that is not in that table is not covered, even if it looks similar.

What "one rule set" means, exactly. The extraction filter's own patterns (quality.credential_spans) drive the prompt mask, the withheld values and the node filter. The extraction prompt then also goes through redact_secrets (redact.py, unchanged). Since stage 10, every substring redact_secrets masks in that prompt, meaning in clean_message(text) and in the masked text before clean_message drops lines, is added to the withheld values. They are found by comparing the text before and after redact_secrets. Not unioned: what redact_secrets would mask in the raw text, which is not what the model sees (for example "hibiscus44&v=1" in "?api_key=hibiscus44&v=1", where the prompt already shows "?api_key=[REDACTED]&v=1"). The node filter itself checks only the extraction filter's patterns plus find_secrets, not every redact_secrets rule. A queued error message is scrubbed of withheld values before it is written to memory_queue.

What the fuzz tests scan, exactly. Counts were measured with len(fuzz_cases()), len(fuzz9_cases()), len(fuzz10_cases()) and len(fuzz11_cases()) and match what each test prints under pytest -s. The stage-8 and stage-9 tests take their labels from the label list, so their size grows with it. (The stage-9 docs said 64,680 for the stage-8 test; that was computed by hand with a wrong label count. The measured count then was 62,720.)
children: Stage 8 (test_extraction_stage8.py): 70,560 combinations (36 labels x 0-6 filler words x 7 connectors x 5 value shapes x 8 message shapes). It checks the extraction prompt, the stored nodes and every file under each combination's own temporary home and database (memory.db, -wal, -shm). Its model always returns valid output, so it never writes memory_queue.

Stage 9 (test_extraction_stage9.py): 20,032 combinations (36 labels x 13 connectors x 5 Unicode variants x 8 message shapes = 18,720, the 5 value shapes taken in turn rather than as a factor; plus 36 labels x 4 JSON / dict / nested JSON / URL query forms x 8 shapes = 1,152; plus 4 URL schemes x 5 value shapes x 8 shapes = 160). Every third combination gets invalid output, so 5,334 really write memory_queue, and every file under the home is scanned.

Stage 10 (test_extraction_stage10.py): 5,769 combinations (36 labels x 16 quoted, wrapped, YAML, Markdown, query and with/using families x 9 message shapes including a ~~~ fence = 5,184; plus 13 curl, CLI, login and token families x 5 value shapes x 9 shapes = 585). 1,923 really write memory_queue. For token shapes it scans for the whole token.

Stage 11 (test_extraction_stage11.py): 5,391 combinations (36 labels x 14 families: nested ( ) [ ] < > { }, wrapped labels before filler, with/using + quoted value, changed ... to, 's / as, XML, YAML |2, x 9 message shapes = 4,536; plus 19 curl, CLI, env-name, login, JSON list / Authorization, Basic and token families x 5 value shapes x 9 shapes = 855). 1,797 really write memory_queue.

Stages 12 and 13 add no fuzz test, only exact tests. Stage 12: each of its 11 cases (len(C_CASES)) checks the exact mask_credentials output, the withheld set and the prompt, and runs a hostile model once with valid and once with queued output, scanning the stored nodes, memory.db and memory_queue; its 6 false positives (len(C_FALSE_POSITIVES)) only check mask_credentials(text) == text and are not run through extraction. Stage 13: the same for its 11 cases (len(A_CASES)) and 4 false positives (len(A_FALSE_POSITIVES)), plus one test that runs clean_extraction and keeps a node holding the ordinary short word "frag". The four fuzz counts above were measured again after stage 13 and did not change.

All four report 0 leaks. None creates a session log: extraction never writes one, and session logs belong to the working layer (gap 3 below). Before each stage, its own matrix leaked on the code it replaced: stage 9's in 5,261 of 7,336 combinations, stage 10's in 4,063 of 5,193 (on 98f6829, 32 labels), stage 11's in 4,562 of 5,391 (on 0e057e4).

knownGaps.text: Short token-shaped values. Short token-shaped values below a pattern's minimum length are not masked (for example glpat-7sd5, whsec_rn6b, a 3-character padded base64): token shapes are recognized by length, so real tokens are not affected, but a short secret in these forms is not covered. The minimums are in the table's "minimum length" column. The substitution check above did not re-test values with special characters or spaces.

Single-= base64 in one case after a label (stage 15). A value with one = of padding that is all lower-case, all upper-case, or capitalised only at the start, directly after a label and followed by more words or another line, is not masked: its = is read as the connector and the words after it are masked instead. Checked: "my token enp6eno= for Trail Tracker", "my token enp6enp6eno= for Trail Tracker", "my token QUFBQUE= for Trail Tracker", "my token Abcdefg= for Trail Tracker" and "my token enp6eno=" followed by a line "Trail Tracker deploys nightly." all leak to the prompt, a stored node and memory_queue, and so do 8-, 12- and 20-character values of each case (tests/memory/test_extraction_stage15.py, 33 strict xfails). Shorter one-case values (4 to 6 characters before the =, "my token abcd= for Trail Tracker") leak the same way. Not affected: == padding in any case, a single = at the end of the message, mixed-case values (row 21), and a value after a real connector ("api key is enp6eno= ...", "secret: ...", "password is ..."). The fix that was tried, treating 7+ base64 characters plus a single = directly after a label as the secret, also captured real filler words ("api key staging= x") and made the stage 9 fuzz leak in 64 combinations, so it was not applied.

knownGaps.text: Why best-effort, and why only exact forms are claimed. Independent reviewers invented new bypasses quickly: the second review found about 45 leaks in 56 new inputs, and each later round found about 30 new variants of shapes that were already handled (the fourth review found 21 leaks in forms the docs claimed). That is why this is a best-effort filter and not a guarantee, and why since stage 12 only the exact verified examples in Handled forms (tested) are claimed.

Recall cost (security over recall). A sentence that matches the rule (a label, a connector and a value) is masked and its node dropped. The longer label list makes this more common: "the token is valid for one hour", "the key point of Trail Tracker is speed", "the pass is valid until June", "auth is handled by Auth0", "the cookie banner is ugly" and "I set the token to expire hourly" all lose their value, and a glued upper-case name ending in KEY masks any value ("MONKEY=banana"). A value after =, and a value on a later line after :, is masked to the end of its clause.

A credential variable whose name is not on the suffix list, such as LUMEN_KEY, is stored as a name ("Rotate LUMEN_KEY for Lumen Budget"); its value is never stored. This is the price of keeping PRIMARY_KEY, and it is why the held-out control group dropped in round 3 (see the table).

Gap 3 (closed for new working notes). Working notes are now masked with the extraction filter's credential mask, in extraction's order, before they are written (see Working layer): verified forms only, with the same "Verified means" definition and minimum lengths as Handled forms (tested), and every gap in this list applies to them too, including the stage 15 one-case single-= base64 gap. room/memory/redact.py itself is unchanged. Only secret-shaped values are scrubbed across turns (the rule is under Working layer); the cases that remain open are listed there and kept as strict xfails. Not covered: those boundaries, and notes written before this change whose session is not captured again with a new turn (they expire 14 days after their last update, and room working purge --all deletes every note). room working promote copies a note's turns as stored, so promoting an older note copies its older redaction.

A fact before a question is kept only when a comma separates it from the question and it opens with a factual marker. These lose a real fact (checked): "I prefer Rust so which parser should I pick?" (no comma), "I joined Corvid Analytics last week, what should I read?" (no marker), "Since we were acquired by Stripe, what changes?" ("were" counts as hypothetical), and "Since I moved to Go if that matters, which linter?" ("if" anywhere in the clause). When unsure, nothing is kept.

The hypothetical check is a word list, so it also catches plain questions that use "could" or "would": "Which database could Harbor Log use?" and "Would Harbor Log work on Fly.io?" no longer keep the Harbor Log project (checked; a missing fact, not a false one).
A hypothetical written without "?" is not seen as a question: "If I build Harbor Log" can still store a Harbor Log project (checked).

An impersonal question that names your project with a single word ("Is Postgres right for Ledgerly?") is dropped: without knowing your projects, "Ledgerly" looks like "Python". Only multi-word Title Case names pass.
"Describe X?" and "Tell me about X?" are not recognised as questions at all, so they reach the model, which is told not to record general knowledge.
